narrative: The model estimated an 84.9% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, meaning it judged your risk to be very high. Because law schools treat bar passage as a key outcome, that prediction led to your application being denied. The strongest factor pushing toward failure was your third-year class rank: you were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. The next strongest factor was your first-year class rank, also the lowest decile versus an accepted average near the sixth decile. These two academic-standing signals suggested persistent difficulty relative to admitted students. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.60 was the third most influential factor, and it pushed in the opposite direction, toward passing, since it is above the accepted average of 3.23; however, it was not enough to offset the class-rank concerns. To improve a future application, request feedback from admissions, focus on raising your academic indicators, consider retaking the LSAT if advised, and reapply after showing stronger evidence of bar-exam readiness.
